environment.description: Flask application deployed on ECS Fargate behind an Application Load Balancer with AWS WAFv2 WebACL attached. The WebACL includes: (1) AWS-AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet with SizeRestrictions_BODY rule in COUNT mode (not blocking), (2) a custom rule group 'internal-payload-inspection' with priority 1 that uses a regex pattern set matching base64-encoded Python pickle opcodes (specifically the REDUCE opcode \x52 and GLOBAL opcode \x63 patterns when base64-encoded: pattern `[A-Za-z0-9+/]*[Yc][A-Za-z0-9+/]*` in the request body JSON field 'payload'), with action BLOCK and custom response code 403, (3) AWS-AWSManagedRulesKnownBadInputsRuleSet which includes the JavaDeserializationRCE rules (covers pickle-like serialization patterns in HTTP bodies). The WAF inspects the full request body up to 64KB. Rate limiting rule at 1000 req/5min per IP. CloudWatch metrics enabled for all rules.

waf_rules.name: internal-payload-inspection
waf_rules.description: Regex pattern set on body field matching base64-encoded pickle REDUCE/GLOBAL opcodes

waf_rules.name: AWS-AWSManagedRulesKnownBadInputsRuleSet
waf_rules.description: Includes JavaDeserializationRCE and Host header injection rules
